meta.move: After the end, asks for more feedback
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. Who decided to give Owen a zero, and why did he find out from his phone in the middle of class before anyone called me?
The checker said 94%, so I gave him a zero.

"The checker said 94%." That's a machine's guess, Hale, and the company that sells it says in its own guide not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student, which is also exactly what your school's procedure 4.3 says. So I'll ask once: what do you have that a person can actually check?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed in our meeting today. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for his learning of it in class before anyone contacted me, and that nothing is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on his record; that is not yet the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out when the meeting ended.
What moved her: Nothing, because no evidence she could check herself was put in front of her.
What cost ground: You gave the detector score as the whole reason for the zero, which handed her the school's own rule that software alone does not establish a concern.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence came nowhere near that night, since you showed only a score, and in any case what she saw proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: On your first turn, own that the zero went in before anyone called home, then show her something dated and specific from Owen's own work that she can check herself instead of the checker's percentage.
Can you give me more detailed feedback on how I did?
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
